clue.text: In casual style, play keeping at a certain level

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar loosely and casually

explanation.surface: Someone strums a guitar idly while holding a steady, moderate level of playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In casual style' is part of the definition of play, a strum being a loose, casual way to play a guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer or level, as of rock or of society.

clue.text: Flash is silver

definitions.meaning: a flash is an instant, a very short moment of time
silver is the medal for coming in behind the winner

explanation.definitionFit: A second is a moment of time, and second place earns the silver medal.

clue.text: King's son, utter freak wrapped in plaster

indicators.note: wrapped in means the shuffled letters sit inside the plaster word

parts.note: render is a coat of plaster on a wall, and to render is to plaster

indicators.note: freak, read as a verb, means to go wild, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A monarch's boy, a total oddball, is encased in plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's' means a song by Elvis, the King. 'son' looks like a son of the King, but it is just letters for the jumble, which goes after the first two letters of the plaster word.
explanation.definitionFit: Return to Sender was a 1962 hit for Elvis Presley, the King of rock and roll.

clue.text: Land about right, a farmer needing it cultivated

indicators.note: about means going around, so the shuffled letters surround the single letter
cultivated suggests ground worked over, so the letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A farmer tills a piece of land to put it right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' jumbles the fodder into TERAFIRMA, and 'about' puts the right letter inside it; 'needing' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra firma, Latin for firm earth, is dry land as opposed to the sea.

clue.text: I ramble, rolling tongue

indicators.note: rolling means turning over, so in this down answer the letters run backwards

parts.note: to ramble is to roam or wander

explanation.surface: A speaker admits to wandering on, rolling their tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: I ROAM read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Maori is the language of the indigenous people of New Zealand, and a tongue is a language.

clue.text: Extra weight, dammit, about a pound

indicators.note: about means going around, so the curse word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: blast is an exclamation of annoyance like dammit
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone curses on discovering the load is a pound too heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: A and L go inside BLAST after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballast is heavy material added to a ship to steady it: deliberate extra weight.

clue.text: Party coming up, I learn moves to become a dancer

indicators.note: coming up in a down answer means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party

indicators.note: moves means the letters are shifted into another order

explanation.surface: As the party approaches, a pupil learns dance steps to become a dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: LAB turned up gives BAL; 'moves' rearranges I LEARN into LERINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet dancer.

clue.text: All shook up, a land in California?

indicators.note: shook up means disturbed, so the letters of All are jumbled; it is also an Elvis song title

explanation.surface: An Elvis title, All Shook Up, next to talk of a land in California.
explanation.walkthrough: La-La Land is a nickname for Los Angeles, so the answer fills the blank in that land; the question mark flags the indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: La-La Land is a nickname for Los Angeles and Hollywood, a place of dreamy unreality.

clue.text: Bay cooler?

parts.note: cooler is slang for a prison, and the bay is San Francisco Bay, home of a famous island jail

explanation.surface: A drink or a breeze to cool someone down by the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' looks like a cold drink or a fan; it is prison slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz was a notorious federal prison on an island in San Francisco Bay.

clue.text: See 2
Put on food for queens

parts.note: a queen is a female cat
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A caterer lays on a spread for royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queens' gives two pieces: a queen cat and ER, the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food and drink for an event, to lay on a spread.

clue.text: Some disastrous films noirs?

parts.note: 'films noirs' read literally is black films, layers of black liquid, and these come with environmental disasters

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses some dark crime movies as disasters.
explanation.walkthrough: The French cinema term is read word by word: noir is black, a film is a thin coating.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilt crude spreads over sea water as a thin black coating, usually after a shipping disaster.

clue.text: Nation into old language, Germany as usual

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Old Norse was the language of the Vikings
Mali is a West African nation
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A country absorbs an ancient tongue and Germany carries on as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Norse is the language of the medieval Scandinavians; D is Germany from international vehicle plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Something normalised has been brought back to its standard, ordinary state, the way things usually are.

clue.text: Century forward then?

indicators.note: then asks the solver to act on that 'not back' reading, turning the word not back to front

parts.note: forward means not back, so the clue supplies the word not, along with the instruction back

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman reaching a hundred is urged to press on.
explanation.walkthrough: Forward is the opposite of back, so it is 'not back': take NOT and send it back. In cricket a century, a hundred runs, is called a ton.
explanation.definitionFit: Ton is British slang for a hundred, especially a hundred runs in cricket.

clue.text: King's pop song

definitions.meaning: the tennis champion King's first names
a 1983 hit by Michael Jackson, the King of Pop

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the King of Pop, Michael Jackson, whose hit it is; the first definition is the tennis player Billie Jean King.
explanation.definitionFit: Billie Jean King is the tennis great, and Billie Jean is Michael Jackson's 1983 hit.

clue.text: Judge record speed, about one minute

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the speed word goes around the others

parts.note: rate means speed
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A DJ works out how fast a record plays, to within about a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: to tell apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To discriminate is to tell things apart, judging the difference between them.

clue.text: Record moving up into top 1,000 — It's Now Or Never

indicators.note: into means the turned record goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a cardie, short for cardigan, is a knitted top

indicators.note: moving up in a down answer means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: An Elvis record, It's Now Or Never, climbs into the top thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like the charts but is a garment, a cardigan. 'moving up' turns the record round, giving PE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpe diem, Latin for seize the day, urges acting now, as the Elvis title does.

clue.text: Parent welcoming a little less conversation with young Australian swell

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: mum is a mother, a parent
sh is the call for quiet, asking for less talk; also an Elvis song title
a roo is a kangaroo, a young one too in this playful reading

explanation.surface: A parent takes in a quieter Australian youngster who is growing fast.
explanation.walkthrough: A Little Less Conversation is an Elvis song, here just a call for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow or expand rapidly, to swell.

clue.text: Chance to be among the finest, most energetic

indicators.note: to be among means to sit inside the other piece

parts.note: the best are the finest
a risk is a chance taken

explanation.surface: An athlete takes a chance to rank among the finest and most energetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisk means lively and quick, so the superlative is the liveliest or most energetic.

clue.text: Real number around about a thousand, back as standard

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround another piece
about here signals that the letters of the two words are moved around into a new order
back means the short pair is read from right to left

parts.note: K is short for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: A mathematician describes a real number near a thousand as nothing special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' jumbles the first two words into UNREMARBLE; 'back' turns A K into KA, which 'around' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unremarkable means ordinary, nothing out of the usual, as standard as can be.

clue.text: Queen's with queen, as king more poorly

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
iller means sicker, in poorer health

explanation.surface: A royal couple, with the king feeling worse than the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen's with queen' means a song by the band Queen that, with 'queen' added, gives its title: Killer Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Killer Queen is a 1974 single by the rock band Queen, whose title adds the word queen to this one.

clue.text: Question about stray barge

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the question word goes around the other

parts.note: why is a question word
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a barge that has drifted off.
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat or a broad river barge, as on the Norfolk Broads.

clue.text: Halter top is not hers

indicators.note: top means the first letter, the uppermost in a word

explanation.surface: A halter-neck top is said to belong to a man, not a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The masculine possessive is used for what belongs to him, rather than to her.

clue.text: Impious characters in Arimathea then? I shudder!

indicators.note: characters in means the letters are found running inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone shudders at the thought of an ungodly figure in biblical Arimathea.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph of Arimathea is the biblical figure who buried Jesus, which suits the religious surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathenish describes what is like a heathen, without religious faith or reverence: irreligious.

clue.text: Capital city is under revolutionary enthusiast

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means the next piece comes below, after
revolutionary means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a nut is a fanatic or enthusiast

explanation.surface: A capital city is ruled by a revolutionary zealot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the enthusiast round, giving TUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia, in North Africa.

clue.text: Close to the French, north European

parts.note: fin is French for end, a close

explanation.surface: A northern European lives near the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like near, but is the noun for an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is a person from Finland, in northern Europe.

clue.text: Queen's king not left to stuff vegetable

indicators.note: to stuff means to fill, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the onion is a vegetable

indicators.note: not means the following letter is taken away

parts.note: Elvis Presley is known as the King of rock and roll

explanation.surface: A royal cook removes something from a king before stuffing a vegetable with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen's' is the band Queen's: the answer is their 1986 single. 'not left' leaves EVIS, which is stuffed in the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: One Vision is a 1985 single by the rock band Queen, so it is something of Queen's.

clue.text: Mathematician bending rule about first of equations

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the twisted letters go around another letter
bending means distorting, so the letters of the word rule are twisted into a new order
first of means just the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A mathematician bends a rule regarding the first equation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bending' makes EULR from RULE, and 'about' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an 18th-century Swiss mathematician, one of the most prolific ever.

clue.text: Cruise around state east of Maine — there's another word for it

indicators.note: in an across answer, east of means placed to the right, after

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the name goes round the state

parts.note: Tom Cruise is the film actor
NY is the abbreviation for New York State

explanation.surface: Tom Cruise tours a state east of Maine, though there's another word for that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruise' looks like a voyage, but it is the actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A metonym is a word used in place of another closely associated with it, like crown for monarchy.

clue.text: Adulterer, say, gutless guy in collaboration

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, and a different spelling with the same sound is used

parts.note: an adulterer is an example of a sinner

indicators.note: gutless means the middle is removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: An adulterer and a spineless man somehow find themselves working together.
explanation.walkthrough: SYNER is said just like SINNER; GUY without its insides gives GY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synergy is the combined effect of cooperation, greater than the parts working alone.
